name: linux-service-start
title: Start a stopped enabled service
description: Starts one systemd service that is enabled at boot but not running (systemctl start). Units that are not enabled, and anything that is not a .service, are refused.
measure: props=$(systemctl show -p ActiveState -p Result -p Type -p RemainAfterExit -p ExecMainStartTimestampMonotonic -p ExecMainPID -p ExecMainCode -p ExecMainStatus -p SuccessExitStatus -- "$unit" 2>/dev/null)
if [ "$enabled" != enabled ]; then arh_blocker "Only services enabled at boot are started here; $unit is ${enabled:-unknown}"; fi
# a one-shot is done only when it ran since boot and systemd counted that run a success. systemd starts every unit with Result=success and
# reset-failed sets it back, so the exit is checked too: ExecMainStatus is the raw status (ExecMainCode 1 an exit, 2 a signal), and a success
# is exit 0, an exit code or signal listed in SuccessExitStatus=, or a failure of the command, marked ExecStart=-, whose pid is ExecMainPID
if [ "$type" = oneshot ] && [ "$remain" = no ] && [ "$state" = inactive ] && [ "$result" = success ] && [ "${ran:-0}" != 0 ]; then
2:[0-9]*) sig=$(kill -l "$code" 2>/dev/null); case " $okexit " in *" ${sig:-x} "*|*" SIG${sig:-x} "*) finished=yes ;; esac ;;

if [ "$finished" = no ] && [ "$pid" != 0 ] && systemctl show -p ExecStart -- "$unit" 2>/dev/null | sed -n "s/^ExecStart={ .* ; ignore_errors=\([a-z]*\) ; start_time=\[[^]]*] ; stop_time=\[[^]]*] ; pid=$pid ; code=.*/\1/p" | grep -qx yes; then finished=yes; fi
if [ "$state" = active ]; then arh_plan false "Already running"
elif [ "$finished" = yes ]; then arh_plan false "Ran and finished (a one-shot service)"
